name: Low Step-Up

instructions.description: Face a stable step and place one whole foot on it.
Lean slightly forward and press through the elevated foot.
Stand on the step without pushing strongly from the trailing foot.
Lower under control and repeat before changing sides.

performanceMetrics.notes: Use a consistent reviewer-defined quality scale for control and alignment.

variations.variationDescription: Low Step-Up — Tempo-Controlled Version: Use a deliberately slower lowering phase without creating a separate database record.
Low Step-Up — Reduced-Range Version: Use a smaller comfortable range while preserving the same movement pattern.

commentsNotes: Select a stable step height that permits controlled ascent and descent.
